Definition: from G1722 and a derivative of G43; to take in one's arms, i.e. embrace:--take up in arms.
BiblicalUsage: To take up in one's arms. Jesus takes a child in His arms in Mark 9:36 and sets him in the midst of the disciples, and He takes the little children up in His arms and blesses them in Mark 10:16.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus taking children into His arms is the gospel in miniature — the kingdom belongs to those small enough to be carried, and I want to be carried too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
